title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.838706: dy formed in prod's registers, and R = 2^26 table rows

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.838706 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on bradcush's 7dd2c482 (125.847937) with two changes. First, loop A (both copies) keeps only the arrival and dx, and prod loads y(T) and y(W) and forms dy in the registers its first product reads, so dy is never stored or reloaded; no walk's point record is written between its arrival and prod (proof.md 2.5). Second, the table has R = 2^26 rows (as in kaankolcu's 850e11fe; BFI of bits 0..26 of y0, P' = 0x3fffe17), so the 2-cycle rate is 1/(6R) = 2^-28.585; h = 0.000048 and p0 = 0.3900482. Per walk: loop A 39.515625 (43.03125 in compare rounds, so compare rounds cost 3.515625 more per walk, a hard row), prod 171.515625, pass 2 339.515625; step 550.546875 + 25647/2^20 = 550.5713 instructions. Walk 0 is an ordinary slot (prod starts from acc = 1); the reserve is 336 milli-units per walk for at most 15 exits and one rare-path entry; the zero-test re-run is its own 2^19-unit action; a doubling is priced at step + 677. The declared run executes pass1, prod and pass2 on 139 production walks with 0 mismatches against big-integer affine secp256k1; both copies of loop A with 0 mismatches against big-integer dx and the address rule; arrive.s with 0 mismatches against the bit-exact model and the exact rule; and all 1,935 + 258 exit stubs on constructed inputs with 0 mismatches against the Python limb ports and big-integer differences. kappa = 1.0001 follows from the shipped hazard census: eleven walk rows, one of them at R = 2^26 (proof.md 5.2). Declared dependencies (proof.md section 6): 7dd2c482, 850e11fe, 886e6f54, a00774d8, c06f6691, 4ac17b66, 445f9a1c, cbea87bf, 4c8222cc, 673640ef, 0a1c5772, 5f1ae3ce, 4595bad7, 01488655, 2bd168b5, daf2c741, a9297fb0, 807e4bf5, b5de673a, 02feb284. Recovery probability is at least 0.39000009 > 0.39 (failure rows < 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory < 2^72 bytes; preprocessing capped at 2^59 units and included; no advice. Exact ledger (rounded up): S_ops = 1.0001*S0 < 2^126.6995024, phase 1 < 2^125.838504, hard extras < 2^111.798282, random extras < 2^97.8873, allowance < 2^112.2339, W_ledger < 2^125.8387053 <= 1000*2^125.838706 milli-units; Markov ratio at most 0.0000476718 (exact, rounded up; the declared run's float ledger, with its cycle rates rounded up, prints 0.0000476737) < 0.000048; certificate.py checks the claim and that 125.838705 fails, in exact arithmetic. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail phases, compares every 128th round) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with node routing, a check that the old and the production compare rule reach the same endpoints, and an optional long-trail trap test (long_trails, not set in the declared run); kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped loops (with rare exits on constructed inputs entering every stub), both copies of the fused pass (loop A: arrival and dx), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
